Max Ammo is the total ammunition capacity of the Herc for that individual weapon.  Each weapon is supplied by separate ammunition.
Current Ammo is the remaining number of shots for that weapon.

alt: Restore the Bioderm's Genetic Stability to its normal level. Stability is lost when a Bioderm's Herc is hit, or when the Bioderm is hit directly. Stability is also lost with each dose of Jackup Stimgland administered. Stability deteriorates every turn once the Toxin threshold is exceeded. When the Bioderm loses half its Stability it begins to turn  blue, and its skill ratings will drop slightly. Once Stability drops below 0, skill ratings drop sharply.  When a skill rating reaches 0%, the Bioderm will be unable to perform that task.

alt: Remove all toxins from this Bioderm.  Toxin buildup occurs only through the use of Stimgland. The two types of Stimgland are Jackup and Placidex.  Jackup increases a Bioderm's chance to hit with weapons, but lowers Genetic Stability.  Placidex rejuvenates lost Stability, but twice as much is needed to counter Jackup's Stability loss.  Once the Toxin threshold is exceeded, additional doses of Stimgland will produce no further beneficial effects. alt:
The two numbers show the Bioderm's current health and potential health. 

Health is lost when a Bioderm's Herc is hit, or when the Bioderm is hit directly. Health deteriorates incrementally when the Bioderm's toxin threshold is exceeded, or when the Bioderm's Genetic Stability drops below its Instability threshold. Certain corrosive atmospheres will damage health each turn if Life Support has been damaged or, in some cases, completely destroyed.  When Health reaches 0%, the Bioderm is dead. 

Health can be completely restored with the Regeneration option in the Medvat.  Health is restored incrementally by more advanced Life Support devices, but very slowly.

alt:
The two numbers show the Bioderm's current genetic stability and potential genetic stability. 

Stability is lost when a Bioderm's Herc is hit, or when the Bioderm is hit directly. Stability is also lost with each dose of Jackup Stimgland administered. Stability deteriorates every turn once the Toxin threshold is exceeded.  When the Bioderm approaches the Instability threshold it begins to turn blue, and its skill ratings will drop slightly. Once Stability drops below the Instability threshold, skill ratings drop sharply.  When a skill rating reaches 0%, the Bioderm will be unable to perform that task. 

Stability can be completely restored with the Stabilize option in the Medvat.  Stability is restored incrementally by more advanced Life Support devices, but very slowly. Placidex Stimgland rejuvenates lost Stability but contributes to Toxin buildup.  A Bioderm with Command can rejuvenate lost Stability if it is within three hexes of the Bioderm at the beginning of the turn. This effect is cumulative.

alt:
The two numbers show the Bioderm's current toxin level and toxin threshold. 

Toxin buildup occurs only through the use of Stimgland. The two types of Stimgland are Jackup and Placidex.  Jackup increases a Bioderm's chance to hit with weapons, but lowers Genetic Stability.  Placidex rejuvenates lost Stability, but twice as much is needed to counter Jackup's Stability loss.  Once the Toxin threshold is exceeded, additional doses of Stimgland will produce no further beneficial effects.  The Bioderm will lose Health and Stability every turn until treated in the Medvat, or until advanced Life Support lowers the Toxin level below the threshold. 

Toxins can be completely removed with the Detox option in the Medvat.  Toxins are removed incrementally by more advanced Life Support devices, but very slowly.

The same tri-nitrogen compound responsible for the brilliant terrain discoloration on Parsus causes a buildup of inert gases in Bioderm respiratory tissues.  This would eventually create a condition similar to nitrogen narcosis, quickly asphyxiating a Bioderm operating without minimal Life Support. 
Though much of the topography on Parsus is made up of gradual changes in elevation, there are enough cliffs to provide adequate defense. Smoother ground allows easier movement.  Rough or jagged terrain is more difficult to cross, and upsets targeting.

The planet Beran is an anomaly.  Its orbit has an average radius of 300 million miles, yet it is a completely developed Terra class world with atmosphere and vegetation.  There is evidence to suggest that Beran and Brell may be terraformed planets. 
Changes in elevation on Beran are gradual, providing little obstructive cover. There are enough trees and boulders, however, to provide some defense. Hercs should move well over hard rock, while icy terrain and swamps provide poor fighting conditions.

Mardalla is the larger of Beran's two moons, and younger by 500 million years. This moon's age may be insufficient for the generation of complex ore deposits.  Its size and an unusually dense core enable it to retain a hospitable gravity, an electromagnetic field and even a minimal atmosphere.  Because Mardalla is heavily composed of toxic metallic compounds, its atmosphere would soon poison a Bioderm that is not protected by a Life support system.  Its high metallic content is also responsible for terrain discoloration. 
Deep pits in Mardalla's surface provide excellent cover for hit-and-run tactics, provided the enemy is not within movement range. Some plant life and boulders can be used defensively.  Some metallic compounds within the terrain melted during this planet's formation, leaving a smooth surface that is easily traversed.

Tirith is smaller and older than its neighbor moon, Mardalla.  This moon's heavily cratered surface attests to its advanced age.  It has been proposed that Tirith is actually a meteor captured by Beran's gravity.  In this event, the potential exists for a greater number of ore deposits being present than a normal moon. 
Extremely gradual changes in elevation offer few strategic opportunities.  Huge craters may provide some defense but will upset targeting.  Smooth terrain affords easier movement, while jagged or rough terrain hinders movement and targeting ability.

The planet Brell is an even greater mystery than its neighbor, Beran. Brell is over 500 million miles from its sun, yet it hosts an even lusher ecology than Beran.  The mountainous jungle terrain of this world is fed by a network of rivers.  Early data concerning Brell indicated a planet covered by desert.  If this is true, Brell may have been terraformed by the Cybrids. 
Varied elevations on Brell provide some degree of cover.  Much of the larger plant life offers some defense as well.  Water is difficult to move through and is a defensive disadvantage.  Jagged terrain hinders movement and targeting ability.

Ora was the site of the Mox Tarsus mining colony.  Its erratic terrain and heavy Cybrid infestation have made this moon difficult to mine. 
Varied elevations on Ora provide some strategic cover.  Smoother ground allows easier movement. Rough or jagged terrain is more difficult to cross, and upsets targeting.

Dirol is another example of a planet that is probably a captured asteroid. It is dense enough to exert a Terra-class gravitational field.  Most of Dirol's surface is covered with ice, possibly composed of frozen gases. 
Varied elevations on Dirol's glaciers provide some strategic cover, though movement on ice is slower and hinders targeting.

Continuous volcanic activity, combined with Hyperion's proximity to the star Ionis, keep the planet's surface temperature high enough to quickly kill a Bioderm without minimal Life Support. 
Hyperion's topography provides some degree of cover.  Many of the larger cinder cones can be used defensively as well.

The planet Dorn was most likely a Terra-class world at one time. Oxidation and nitrate depletion have destroyed any native life, though Dorn's atmosphere will remain breathable for several millenia. Sudden changes in elevation may be the result of internal instability.  Dorn's two moons are Odon and Dobo. 
Extremes in elevations have earned Dorn the nickname "Maze world." These natural formations provide strategic advantages.  Dead trees and boulders could also be used defensively, if needed.  Polarized amber, found only on Dorn, may somehow aid weapon performance.

Veins of a pyrite-based compound can be found running throughout Odon. In the "Corporate mythos" of the splinter faction that discovered this system, Odon and Dobo were the sons of a great leader, Dorn, who was assassinated by his rivals.  The sons avenged his death by destroying all of Dorn's enemies, and then stood vigil at his tomb until his return.  In the Newspeech of that time, the name Odon meant "the golden one." 
Odon's surface is now baked and dry, destroying any life it once had. The deep gouges in the planet's surface could prove to be death traps due to the hindering effects of the uneven terrain.  Boulders and dead trees may provide enough protection to take control of the surface.

In the "Corporate mythos" of the splinter faction that discovered this system, Odon and Dobo were the sons of a great leader, Dorn, who was assassinated by his rivals.  The sons avenged his death by destroying all of Dorn's enemies, and then stood vigil at his tomb until his return.  In the Newspeech of that time, the name Dobo meant "the aggressive one." 
Deep ravines and pits on this world may provide quick cover in some situations.

The atmosphere of Xhiron is composed primarily of methane and particulate corrosives. Fissures in the planet's surface continuously produce toxic gases, evidence of this world's unstable interior. Xhiron's six moons are Basmalt, Tahn, Kabulov, Ursk, Muynak, and Morav. 
Xhiron's frozen gas glaciers present excellent strategic opportunities for hit-and-run tactics. Their elevation prevents line of sight, and crossing over them is difficult due to gravity and icy terrain.

Like Dorn, Basmalt was probably a completely Terra-class world.  A shift in this planet's orbit resulted in the destruction of any native life.  Continuous tectonic activity has resulted in a mostly uniform topography.  Basmalt's atmosphere is considered toxic. 
Basmalt's gradual changes in elevation provide little cover.  Movement along its rocky ridges proves easier than its sandy floor.  Ancient alien artifacts on this planet may have a positive effect on weapons systems.

Tahn is a large enough moon to retain a sufficient gravity field and a breathable atmosphere.  It has a lush jungle environment dense enough to discourage colonization in some cases.  Heavy Cybrid infestation is indicated.  This moon is apparently of particular interest to the Cybrids, perhaps because of its electromagnetic fields. 
Changes in elevation on Tahn are more gradual than they appear.  Trees and related plant life are the major defensive elements this world has to offer.  Bodies of water are made more difficult to cross by exposed rocks.

Extreme caution is advised in exploring this moon.  Little is known about Kabulov because of its extremely inhibiting electromagnetic field.  It has been speculated that an unknown element exists at this moon's core. 
Most of Kabulov appears flat, with occasional unbroken mountain ridges.

Ursk is covered in a sheet of frozen methane and trace minerals.  Its rugged beauty is offset by an inhibiting electromagnetic field and poisonous atmosphere. 
Varied elevations on Ursk's glaciers provide some strategic cover, though movement on ice is slower and hinders targeting.

In geologic terms, Muynak is a very recently formed moon.  Shifting plate tectonics continually release lava flows across its surface.  Muynak's compact wave electromagnetic field has made analysis difficult. 
Gradual changes in elevation offer little cover.  Many of the larger cinder cones can be used defensively.

Morav was seen as an ideal colonization site before Cybrid infestation was discovered. In Newspeech, the name "Morav" meant "Paradise." 
Morav is covered by shallow intersecting rivers.  Its gentle terrain offers little protection, though much of the larger plant life could be used as cover.

Salikh may have lost any breathable atmosphere it once had during its initial formation.  Any water remaining would be at the sub-microscopic level. 
Changes in elevation on Salikh are greater than they appear.  Mesas and spires on this world provide excellent strategic opportunities.

Praab is a tiny jungle planet that should be covered in ice.  The presence of an electromagnetic field with an inhibiting wave signature greatly hindered initial analysis. 
Praab's mountainous terrain offers some strategic elements, though changes in elevation are too gradual to offer much cover.  Trees and boulders offer some protection, and a series of bizarre monoliths found only on Praab seem to be positively polarized.

Robotic probes were destroyed before reaching this planet.  Long range spectral analysis indicates a severely corrosive atmosphere due to the presence of unknown compounds. Heavy volcanic activity is also indicated.  This planet's codename, and those of its moons, refer to ancient legends of an underworld.
Robotic probes were destroyed before reaching this moon.  Long range spectral analysis indicates an extremely corrosive atmosphere due to the presence of unknown compounds.
Robotic probes were destroyed before reaching this moon.  Long range spectral analysis indicates an extremely corrosive atmosphere and an unusually strong gravitational pull.
Paracelsus was the first system explored after Mankind colonized Terra Nova.
